observations.finding: DMSO f_a63b63b85186 is confluent epithelioid monolayer with uniform oval blue nuclei, green filamentous microtubule network and red cortical actin. All 4 treated fields are markedly sparser at identical contrast, with many detached bright yellow-white rounded cells, indicating reduced adherent cell number. No cell-count z-score in top_deviations so not covered by measurements.

Nuclei in all treated fields are irregular, lobulated, fragmented into multiple micronuclei/blue puncta per cell and large polyploid/multinucleated cells visible in f_1807f605c4b6, f_72f3bee2bcec, f_0072fc6616f9, f_5fdd58869bd8 central and lower fields, vs round-oval nuclei in DMSO. Read from blue channel in composite.

Nuclei irregularity matches very strong negative z for nuc_solidity (-30.4 at 10uM 130 cells, -43.8 at 0.3uM 302 cells, DMSO median 0.972 -> 0.96-0.95) and nuc_form_factor (-23.8, -39.4 DMSO 0.916 -> 0.879, 0.855).

Enlarged nuclei/cells with markedly increased DNA content visible as large blue masses with many micronuclei, e.g. clusters in f_0072fc6616f9 and f_5fdd58869bd8 and isolated giant cells in f_72f3bee2bcec.
Large nucleus/DNA increase matches frac_large_nucleus z=14.26 (0.006->0.041) and nuc_dna_integrated z=14.83 (315->505) at 10uM and z=6.27 (315->395) at 0.3uM.
Cell shape more rounded/compact with spiky cortical red actin and reduced spreading vs flat polygonal cells in DMSO; many rounded mitotic-like cells.
Rounding matches cell_roundness z=6.12 (0.525->0.575) at 0.3uM. No grayscale tubulin channel provided, composite limits fine spindle read, but phenotype is cell-cycle/mitotic failure with polyploidy.
Actin (red) appears much brighter and more heterogeneous/contracted at cell cortex and in rounded cells vs diffuse cortical red in DMSO, at identical contrast.
Actin brightness/heterogeneity matches act_mean z=15.25 and 8.70 (0.277->0.708,0.523), act_std z=17.77 and 12.83 (0.073->0.284,0.225), act_glcm_contrast z=21.06 and 7.38 (0.001->0.005,0.003).
Tubulin (green) loses filamentous network, appears diffuse to clumped with bright puncta and increased texture variation in treated fields vs radial green fibers in DMSO.

Tubulin variability matches tub_std z=21.40 (0.108->0.335) and tub_glcm_contrast z=17.60 (0.002->0.004) at 10uM. Composite-only view precludes separate grayscale quantification but texture change visible.

data.note:
Unblinding check: correct. Compound was vincristine (PubChem CID 5978, CHEMBL90555, ChEMBL mechanism Tubulin inhibitor [e15]) annotated in BBBC021 as Microtubule destabilizers. Scientist call Microtubule destabilizers (p=0.78) matches protocol NSC 3/4 vote [e8] with high cosine similarities up to 0.93 to demecolcine reference, scored correct by code.

Reflection: Phenotype was strong mitotic/cytokinesis failure: extreme nuclear irregularity (nuc_solidity z -30 to -47, nuc_form_factor z -23 to -39) plus polyploidy (frac_large_nucleus z 9-16, nuc_dna_integrated z 6-14 at 0.1-10 µM [e2,e3,e6,e7]) with visual large multinucleated/micronucleated cells and bright heterogeneous actin/tubulin texture [e4]. Microscopist favored Aurora kinase inhibitors due to polyploidy but failed to weight quantitative tubulin increase (tub_mean rho=+1.0 p=0 [e11]) and NSC similarity properly. Dose-response showed persistent large-nucleus phenotype with no mitotic_fraction increase [e9,e10], consistent with microtubule destabilizer-induced arrest/slippage rather than acute Eg5 monopolar block.

Literature supports vinca alkaloids as tubulin-binding depolymerizers causing microtubule destabilization: see microtubule-targeting in Ewing sarcoma context (PMID 35803262) and microtubule depolymerization leading to arrest in G1/M (PMID 35436470). Follow-up proposed live tubulin polymerization + p-H3 time-course vs reference compounds would cleanly separate destabilizer from Aurora B phenotype.

reflection.text:
Post-unblinded reflection - vincristine = Microtubule destabilizers / Tubulin inhibitor - verdict CORRECT, scientist_correct true via protocol.

What got it right and why:

1. Acquisition choice was appropriate: list_available_experiments (e1) showed 8 doses (0.003-10 uM) with 4 wells affordable. Sampling w_5a47dd5361 at 10 uM (e2), w_552fc323cc at 0.3 uM (e3), w_af047c92af at 1 uM (e6), w_f8df549b85 at 0.1 uM (e7) covered maximal to low-intermediate dose. This revealed the dose-dependence: 130 cells at 10 uM vs 302-314 cells at 0.1-1 uM, and avoided spending all replicates on one end of the curve.

2. Core morphology was consistent and discriminative: nuc_solidity z = -30.4 at 10 uM, -43.8 to -47.4 at 0.1-0.3 uM, -46.6 at 1 uM; nuc_form_factor z = -23.8 to -39.5; frac_large_nucleus z = +14.3 to +16.7; tub_std z = +21.4 at 10 uM and act_std z = +16.2 at 1 uM. Consistent nuclear irregularity + large-nucleus/polyploidy across all 4 wells is the expected downstream of prolonged mitotic failure/slippage. Lookup (e14/e15) and unblinding confirmed vincristine PubChem 5978, CHEMBL90555, mechanism Tubulin inhibitor, structure agreement, consistent with microtubule destabilizer class.

3. Protocol comparison got it right: first compare_to_reference_atlas over 2 wells (e5) was split - NSC 1/2 Microtubule destabilizers, k-neighbours Eg5 6/10 vs destabilizers 4/10. Second comparison over 4 wells (e8) consolidated to NSC 3/4 Microtubule destabilizers, k-neighbours tie 5/10 each. Per-well protocol (verdict detail) shows why: 0.1 uM similarity 0.93 destabilizer, 0.3 uM 0.919 destabilizer, 1 uM 0.892 destabilizer vs only 10 uM 0.772 Eg5 inhibitors. Summed similarity 2.741 vs 0.772 strongly favours destabilizers over runner-up. update_hypotheses at 0.78 (e12) was well-calibrated given 3/4 not unanimous.

4. Dose-response helped against stabilizer: tub_mean rho = +1.00 p=0 (e11) monotonic increase was used to contradict Microtubule stabilizers (0.02 probability). Flat frac_mitotic_like rho = +0.40 p=0.6 (e9) argued against sustained Eg5 monopolar mitotic arrest, which should enrich mitotic-like fraction.

What was misleading / what I missed:

1. describe_phenotype (e4): microscopist reported density similar vs DMSO and 11 observations favoring Aurora kinase inhibitors. This was composite-only, could not resolve spindle, and explicitly did not exclude tubulin mechanism. I weighted it as contradicting (e12) but it contributed to inflated Aurora probability 0.12. Visually, Aurora B failed-cytokinesis polyploidy and vinca-induced slippage polyploidy are indistinguishable on DAPI alone - both give large irregular nuclei. No free analysis could resolve this; required the tubulin intensity trend and NSC similarities.

2. High-dose outlier: w_5a47dd5361 at 10 uM drove the sole Eg5 vote with low similarity 0.772 and low cell count (toxicity/loss). If I had sampled only high doses I would have been misled. Acquiring low-intermediate wells corrected this.

3. Dose-response limitations: frac_large_nucleus rho = -0.80 p=0.2 (e10) with n=4 wells has no power and trend direction is uninterpretable due to saturation already at 0.1 uM (+16.7). I did not over-interpret it, correctly.

Vincristine is a canonical tubulin inhibitor/microtubule destabilizer PMID 27472259, consistent with mechanisms that disrupt microtubule dynamics and cause mitotic defects PMID 27760837 PMID 35803262 PMID 35436470, a phenotype also seen with other microtubule-targeting agents PMID 36967563. No additional literature needed to overturn NSC vote; next experiment if real lab remains live-cell tubulin polymerization + phospho-H3 timecourse vs references as proposed in e13.

No clinical advice is given; this is phenotypic MoA screening only.
